text:
maria_customer: hey folks — we're seeing streaming responses cut out when clients go through our ALB + Cloudflare stack. first chunk arrives, then after ~28-35s connection closes with partial event. direct calls to the hosted endpoint (no proxy) stream fine. low qps. request id: req_20260315_9a1c. any ideas?

emma_support: thanks for the report — sorry about that. can you paste a minimal repro (curl) + response headers? is the client using EventSource/SSE or websocket fallback?

maria_customer: here's the curl we used: ```curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" "https://our-domain.example/api/v1/stream?prompt=hi" --no-buffer``` response headers we saw (from the proxied response): ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK\ncontent-type: text/event-stream\ntransfer-encoding: chunked\ncache-control: no-cache\ncontent-encoding: gzip\ncf-cache-status: DYNAMIC\nconnection: keep-alive\n``` after ~30s the connection is reset (RST) or client sees EOF.

emma_support: useful — looks like there's gzip + chunked + cloudflare in front. raj_sre can you weigh in on ALB/Cloudflare interactions?

raj_sre: quick checklist: ALB default idle timeout is 60s, should not cut at 30s. Cloudflare sometimes buffers responses if it detects them as not streaming (e.g., gzip + content-length anomalies) and can drop idle streams. nginx/Envoy in front of origin can also buffer and tear down upstream. We should capture tcpdump at the origin-facing side and the ALB-to-origin side to see which hop closes.

lina_prod: we rolled a small nginx change last week that enabled gzip by default for that route (to save bandwidth). nginx config snippet I pushed: ```location /api/v1/stream { proxy_pass http://upstream; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; gzip on; proxy_buffering on; proxy_read_timeout 90s; }``` that might be a smoking gun — proxy_buffering + gzip can convert a streaming response into a buffered one and trigger Cloudflare buffering behavior.

emma_support: good catch. maria, can you try disabling gzip and proxy_buffering (if you control that side) or bypass Cloudflare to test? simple repro commands: ```# bypass CF via host header and origin IP
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Host: our-domain.example" http://ORIGIN_IP:8080/api/v1/stream -H "Accept: text/event-stream"```

maria_customer: tried bypassing CF (hit origin directly) and stream stays open for >5 minutes. so origin looks fine. when going through ALB+CF it dies ~30s.

raj_sre: that narrows it to ALB<->Cloudflare or Cloudflare's edge. Two likely culprits: 1) Cloudflare buffering (they have an option to buffer/unbuffer streaming responses, and gzip+proxy_buffering makes it look non-streaming) 2) an intermediate nginx/ALB idle/reset due to missing TCP keepalive or missing periodic flushes from the app. Do you have server-side SSE heartbeats?

maria_customer: server does not send keepalive heartbeats by default — we rely on token output intermittently. we can add a 15s comment event as heartbeat.

raj_sre: please add a heartbeat first — that will prove whether the path needs periodic bytes to stay alive. Also request Cloudflare support to confirm whether they are buffering the route (attach req_20260315_9a1c).

deploy-bot: deploy completed for service-stream v1.12.3 at 2026-03-15T17:35:20Z (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket: 

emma_support: while we wait, actionable config changes: on nginx/ingress set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and `proxy_send_timeout`/`proxy_read_timeout` increase to 300s. For Envoy, set `stream_idle_timeout: 0s` or a high value and ensure `disable_chunked_encoding: false` isn't enabled. For ALB consider using NLB in front (TCP passthrough) for streaming endpoints or raise ALB idle timeout to 300s.

lina_prod: noted — I'll prepare a small ingress patch and a canary. also adding a short L7 route rule to bypass gzip for /api/v1/stream.

maria_customer: after disabling proxy_buffering and gzip on the ingress and deploying, behavior improved — stream stays open. when we re-enabled gzip+proxy_buffering it closed again at ~32s. so feels like Cloudflare was buffering because the upstream was presenting gzip and buffering.

raj_sre: great repro. root cause: simultaneous gzip + proxy_buffering caused origin to send buffered chunks; Cloudflare treated it as non-stream and applied internal timeouts/cleanup. mitigation: disable response buffering for streaming endpoints, ensure server flushes events immediately (e.g., fflush or flush on write), and add heartbeat comments at 15s intervals. long-term: add a streaming runbook and route-specific ingress profile (proxy_buffering off, no gzip, keepalive pings).

emma_support: next steps assigned: lina_prod to land ingress change + canary (ETA 2h), raj_sre to open a Cloudflare ticket referencing req_20260315_9a1c and ask for clarification about dynamic buffering heuristics (ETA 1h), maria_customer to roll heartbeat patch (ETA 30m) and verify. I'll follow up with a short summary and runbook link.

raj_sre: I'll also add a note to the infra docs: streaming endpoints should have a dedicated L7 profile (proxy_buffering off, proxy_read_timeout > 120s, no gzip) and consider TCP passthrough for customers with heavy streaming needs.

maria_customer: heartbeat deployed, confirmed stable for 10m through ALB+CF. closing from our side. we'll keep monitoring and report if anything pops up.

emma_support: marking thread resolved — we'll follow up with a runbook doc and the ingress PR number when ready. :white_check_mark:
